headline: Majors hold trend structure as short-term price breaks vs. month-long rallies; whales moving onto exchanges while leverage stays crowded and funding cheap.
paragraphs: The regime is intact but showing wear. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and BNB all sit above their 200-day simple moving averages, and all except XRP display golden crosses, meaning their 50-day lines sit above their 200-day lines. That is a bullish scaffold. But the picture fractures at the daily window: Bitcoin down 2.1% on the day and 2.5% on the week, Ethereum down 1.0% on both, Solana down 2.6% on the day and 3.9% on the week. XRP has fallen 4.0% in 24 hours, and the broader index shed 1.67% of total market cap in the same span. Yet over 30 days the narrative flips entirely: Bitcoin up 19.9%, Ethereum up 27.9%, Solana up 34.4%, XRP up 24.8%, BNB up 24.4%. The month-long trend is real; the last week has been a pullback within it. DOGE and ADA tell the same story: both down on the day and week, both up sharply over the month. This is a market pulling back from a rally, not one breaking down.

Momentum has rolled over across the board. Bitcoin RSI sits at 53.1, Ethereum at 58.3, Solana at 53.8, XRP at 50.9, BNB at 55.0, DOGE at 49.2, ADA at 49.9. All are in neutral or overbought territory, yet not one shows MACD above its signal line. That divergence matters: the price trends higher on the month, the oscillators are flat or falling, and the lines have rolled over. This is textbook deceleration within a rally, the kind of rest that either launches the next leg or turns into something longer. Nothing here says the trend is finished, but it is tired.

Leverage is expensive and lopsided. Bitcoin funding on OKX sits at 0.33% per 8-hour period, or 3.6% annualized, the second-highest read across the board after ETH at 0.78% per 8-hour (8.6% annual). That cost to hold long is notable; when funding is positive and rising, longs are paying, which happens when the market is crowded to one side. Bitcoin's long-short ratio is 1.52, meaning 1.52 longs for every 1 short, and Solana runs 2.08. XRP reaches 2.84 longs per short, DOGE 4.2. Those are crowded backsides. However, open interest on Bitcoin sits at 2.2 billion dollars, large but not at cycle extremes for this market. The boat is full, not overflowing. Liquidations over the last hour to three hours have been skewed: Bitcoin saw 495k longs liquidated against 322k shorts, Solana 105k longs against 448k shorts, and XRP 803k longs against 274k shorts. That is not symmetrical; shorts are taking pain in some venues and longs in others, suggesting the market is still searching for balance after the month-long run.

Whales are feeding supply to venues. Over the last 24 hours, 114.98 million dollars of BTC moved net onto exchanges, with the two largest flows being 89.6 million to Coinbase Institutional and 76.5 million to Coinbase retail. Over longer windows the picture is murkier: the week ending August 21 saw 455 million onto exchanges, the week of August 28 saw 1.1 billion onto exchanges, but the week ending September 4 reversed course with 409 million moving off exchanges, and the most recent week ending September 11 swung back to 787 million onto exchanges. That is a saw: onto, onto, off, onto again. The stablecoin float stands at 309.8 billion dollars, up only 1.21% over 30 days despite the month-long rally, meaning demand for buying power has not overwhelmed supply. Spot ETF flows contradict the whale picture on the day: Bitcoin saw a 282.7 million dollar outflow on September 10, while the last five sessions have netted 455.9 million inflow. Ethereum posted a 29.9 million outflow on the day against 147.8 million inflow over five sessions. These two windows are disagreeing, the day negative and the multi-session positive. The traditional finance bid is present but lumpy.

Sentiment reads 56 on the Fear and Greed index, labeled Greed, sitting near the middle of its 30-day range of 29 to 74. The crowd is neither panicked nor euphoric. Difficulty is rising, up 3.0% with 1,170 blocks to the next retarget, suggesting steady hash rate despite price chop. Network fees are minimal at 1 satoshi per byte for both the fastest and hourly rates. The data shows money moving onto venues where price can be tested lower, leverage compressed but not in collapse, and the month-long rally pausing without the technical structure breaking. The specific condition to monitor is whether Bitcoin can hold above its 200-day line through the next pullback, and whether whales continue moving onto exchanges as they have over three of the last four weeks.

The top movers today show dispersion: RAY up 24.98%, VVV up 10.28%, FF up 8.83%, against VET down 6.81%, WLFI down 6.62%, ALGO down 6.23%. The index down 1.67%, individual assets swinging wildly. That chop inside a month-long uptrend is normal, the ebb and flow of money finding new levels. Nothing in this tape points to either capitulation or climax, only a market that has run far and fast and is now resting before the next move, with major players using venue deposits to manage exposure.
